title: Galileo Ventures 6mdash; workload burn & hosting pathways
next_steps: Priya to run three benchmark passes (short/medium/long sequences) across Hosted and Dedicated by 2026-11-20
Evan to share SOC2/ISO artifacts and Private deployment checklist by 2026-11-17
Jordan + Samuel to align on network config and test VPC peering window for 2026-11-18
Maya to provide representative production request traces and SLA targets by 2026-11-15
action_items: Priya Nair: create benchmark harness (10k requests, mix of 128/512/1024 tokens) and run on Hosted + Dedicated configs (due 2026-11-20)
Jordan Lee: draft VPC/private deployment architecture diagram and required firewall rules (due 2026-11-18)
Maya Ortiz: share sample payloads and peak qps expectations (due 2026-11-15)
Evan Park: send pricing bands, pilot contract stub, and links to security pack (due 2026-11-17)
summary: Galileo is evaluating hosting options for a realtime inference feature (token generation + embeddings). Primary decision factors: p95 latency under 200ms for small responses, 99th percentile throughput during billing windows, operator control for data residency, and clear unit-cost targets for monthly burn. Team agreed to run cross-mode benchmarks and reconvene with cost model and security artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Evan Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think well give it about 45 minutes to an hour, go over workload, success criteria, and then the hosting options. Maya, can you kick off with a quick summary of what Galileo is trying to achieve?
[00:18] Maya Ortiz: sure thanks Evan. Were building an assistant that summarizes investor Q&A and generates bullet insights. Typical response length is 80-250 tokens, with occasional long form 800-1k token summaries for reports. Peak qps currently around 70, avg qps 12 during day.
[00:35] Samuel Reed: and to add, we have batch jobs at night that run embeddings over the feed - those are throughput-focused not latency-sensitive.
[00:45] Priya Nair: ok that mix actually maps nicely to Redwoods hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, short responses are latency-sensitive and benefit from low-concurrency fast routing, longer summaries hit cost concerns. Do you have an internal p95 goal?
[00:58] Maya Ortiz: target p95 for short responses is 200ms end-to-end, p99 ideally under 400ms. For the nightly batches we care about cost more than latency, but they should finish within the window we have (2-3 hours).
[01:10] Omar Haddad: also from infra side were constrained on egress and data residency. Customer data cannot leave region X, and security team wants audit logs + KMS integration.
[01:23] Leah Kim: yes and we need SOC2 level controls, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and an expectation of an on-prem option within the next 9-12 months if pilots go well.
[01:35] Jordan Lee: thanks. quick clarifying q: when you say cannot leave region X, is that hard restriction for hosted?
[01:41] Leah Kim: ideally we prefer hosted in region X, but if thats not possible were evaluating Dedicated in a single-tenant pool in region X or Private VPC/on-prem.
[01:53] Evan Park: great context. so we should scope a pilot that exercises three hosting modes: Hosted (region X, standard model), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and Private (VPC or on-prem). main outputs: latency p50/p95/p99, throughput at target qps, and token-unit cost for each mode.
[02:10] [02:10] Priya Nair: ill outline the benchmark plan. step one: synthetic mix to simulate 60 qps with a 70/30 split short/long. step two: peak burst test to 150 qps to observe autoscale/burst behavior. step three: nightly batch run for embeddings. well instrument upstream traces and token counts.
[02:28] Maya Ortiz: curious on the KV cache behavior - in our app most users open multiple threads and we do prefix prompting. how does Redwoods serving runtime handle KV cache across dedicated/shared?
[02:38] Priya Nair: short answer: Dedicated gives you stronger cache locality (same pool), hosting can evict more aggressively due to multi-tenant packing. we can enable prefix caching for all modes but effective hit rate will vary. well include cache-hit metrics in the run.
[02:51] Samuel Reed: on the Dedicated pricing side, how do we think about reserved capacity vs burst? we want predictable cost but also need headroom for spikes.
[02:59] Evan Park: Dedicated is committed capacity with burst credits; for the pilot we suggest a small reserved baseline sized to your typical peak and burst windows configured for up to 2.5x for short periods. well model cost per token for baseline + burst amortized over expected load.
[03:15] Leah Kim: and private on-prem, we need to know the hardware stack requirements. our infra team wants an installable package and network firewall guidance.
[03:24] Jordan Lee: noted, well share the private deployment checklist. for on-prem we support the standard GPU profiles (A100, H100) and have a compact runtime for quantized models if you want lower TCO. well also provide a manifest that lists driver versions and kernel dependencies.
[03:40] Maya Ortiz: model variants question: do you recommend same model across modes or smaller quantized variant on Dedicated/Private?
[03:46] Priya Nair: depends on quality tolerance. we can run the same FP32 baseline on Hosted and Dedicated; for Private you may choose a quantized variant to reduce GPU RAM and cost. well include quality regression checks in the benchmark (BLEU/ROUGE-ish, and human spot checks).
[04:02] Evan Park: lets talk acceptance criteria. what would a successful pilot look like for you, Maya?
[04:08] Maya Ortiz: pass criteria: p95 <= 200ms for short responses in production-like environment, token cost below $0.0007 per token for mixed workload, and SOC2/SSO docs in place. plus a plan to scale to 1k qps within 90 days of pilot signoff.
[04:24] [04:24] Priya Nair: noted. well design the benchmark harness to measure those explicitly. for the p95 target well measure end-to-end (app to model) using our trace headers and sample traces you provide.
[04:36] Samuel Reed: timeline question: were looking to have a pilot decision in 3 weeks, pilot run over 2 weeks, and then expand. is that realistic?
[04:45] Jordan Lee: yes thats plausible. typical cadence: 1 week to provision and baseline, 1 week to run full benchmarks and iterate, then a final decision week. we can compress if you provide traces and an env for testing right away.
[04:58] Leah Kim: security review: we need encryption at rest and in transit, customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and audit log retention for 12 months. do you have those controls today?
[05:09] Evan Park: yes we support TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports an enterprise-tier KMS option, and well share SOC2 report and the audit log schema.
[05:20] Maya Ortiz: any gotchas on data retention or PII scrubbing? we might need to mask certain fields before sending to model.
[05:26] Priya Nair: masking is usually done pre-ingest; Redwood can recommend pre-processing best practices and we can run a token-exposure analysis during the pilot.
[05:36] Evan Park: ok ill summarize next steps at the end. any more technical deep dive items?
[05:41] Samuel Reed: curious about routing/fallbacks. if Hosted is down or overloaded, can requests be routed to Dedicated or a quantized fallback?
[05:48] Jordan Lee: yes we have smart routing policies. we can route by latency budget, cost, and region. automatic fallback to compatible variant is supported; well test that in the burst scenarios.
[05:59] Maya Ortiz: on cost modeling, can you provide a blended cost calculator? we want to compare Hosted unit-cost vs amortized Dedicated vs on-prem TCO.
[06:06] Evan Park: yes we have a cost model template; ill fill in preliminary numbers based on your qps and token mix and share with you.
[06:12] [06:12] Priya Nair: final note on benchmarks: well capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, token counts, cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and cost per token. well also capture model quality metrics on a sampled subset.
[06:28] Leah Kim: for the security packet, please include SSO metadata, audit log retention policy, and the encryption key lifecycle.
[06:34] Evan Park: will do. to close, well have the bench runs done by 2026-11-20, security docs ready by 2026-11-17, and reconvene 2026-11-22 to review results and pick a pilot hosting mode. sound good?
[06:47] Maya Ortiz: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:50] Evan Park: thanks all, well follow up with links to the benchmark harness and a short checklist.
[06:55] [end of meeting]
